findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and raises TypeError when instantiated.
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, so it implements none of the abstract methods: `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Before this change it was a concrete handler whose `evaluate` returned `[]`. `Detector.detector_handler` creates the handler with `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any metric-alert detector run through `process_detectors` would now fail with `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. I couldn't see whether `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` is set to this class; the comment in the file suggests it is. Fix: keep a concrete stub that implements the abstract methods (they can return empty values for now), or don't switch the base class until the handler is implemented.

findings.title: The expected occurrence is built for group key "val1" but the test evaluates "group_key".
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)` sets the fingerprint to `"<id>:val1"`. The handler is then run with `expected_result.group_key == "group_key"`, so its occurrence gets fingerprint `"<id>:group_key"`. The `IssueOccurrence` objects differ, so the equality check on the evaluated result should fail. Pass `"group_key"` when building the expected occurrence.
